vulnerable_statements.reason: MSI/MSI-X teardown and device disable are tied to the same condition. When only the IRQ is being torn down (disable_device == false), the device is still disabled. When the device is disabled, MSI is turned off without coordinating with the hotplug IRQs that child bridges allocated under this slot. In nested-bridge hot-unplug, those child IRQ resources are leaked or left dangling. Later IRQ teardown or reuse then works on freed or inconsistent MSI state, which can crash the kernel.
This is called whenever irq > 0, even when the caller asked not to disable the device. It disables a device that is still in use and breaks the enable/disable reference balance.

suggested_fix: Split MSI teardown from device disable. Add a separate 'disable_msi' parameter: disable MSI/MSI-X only when disable_device or disable_msi is set, and call pci_disable_device() only when disable_device is true. On unplug, make sure the hotplug IRQs of child slots are freed (free_irq, then destroy_workqueue) before the parent's MSI vectors are released. That way no IRQ resources leak or outlive the MSI domain.
